subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - post-call recap
snippet: Recap from today's perf qualification call - p95/p99 targets, concurrency, streaming requirements and next steps.
messages:
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@finlytics.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: performance SLOs (p95/p99) - recap

Thanks again for the call today - really helpful. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can align on the mutual action plan.

Key points we captured:
- Current end-to-end (client -> model -> client) numbers with our provider (averages from last 7 days): p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 890ms for single-turn prompts (~128 tokens).
- Our target for production: p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 500ms for typical interactive flows (median response size ~80 tokens).
- Concurrency: we expect bursts up to 60 concurrent sessions during peak trading hours; sustained baseline ~15-20.
- Throughput: average sustained ~60 req/sec, peak up to 200 req/sec for short windows.
- Streaming requirement: we rely on partial token streaming for faster perceived latency (first byte ideally <120ms).

Open questions:
1) For Redwood hosted API, what p95/p99 can we expect end-to-end (including customer -> Redwood public API -> model -> response) for models you recommended during the call?
2) What are your recommended concurrency/connection pooling settings (per-connection keepalive, multiplexing) to support 60 concurrent sessions without queueing?
3) Any additional guidance on batching/aggregation and how it affects streaming latencies?

Attached: our current-provider metrics export for the last 7 days.

Thanks - Alex
Alex Garcia
Head of Product, FinLytics

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@finlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance SLOs (p95/p99) - recap

Alex - thanks for the clear recap and the attached CSV. I pulled together a short post-call summary and next steps below.

Short answers to your open questions:
1) Redwood hosted API expected e2e numbers (median-sized requests ~80 tokens, streaming enabled): p95 ~ 140-180ms, p99 ~ 260-360ms. These are conservative estimates based on the model variants we discussed (quantized 4-bit optimized variants on our hosted clusters) and typical internet latency from US regions. We can run a dedicated perf test from your infra to validate.
2) For 60 concurrent sessions we recommend: 1 TCP connection per application instance with HTTP/2 multiplexing (or keep 4-8 long-lived connections per process), per-connection request limit ~1000/min; set client-side concurrency pool to ~80 to allow headroom for spikes. Our autoscaling supports burst capacity beyond committed pools if needed.
3) Batching vs streaming: continuous batching reduces per-token cost but increases first-byte latency. For interactive use with streaming, we use small micro-batches (1-4 requests) and prefix/KV cache to keep first-byte latency low. We can tune batching windows per-route.

Attachments: I attached our Redwood performance runbook that outlines typical numbers and tuning knobs. Action items:
- Marissa: schedule a 1-hour perf test run (we'll coordinate load generator from your environment).
- Aditya: prep a short perf profile (p95/p99, first-byte, tail latency) for the recommended model variants.
- Alex/Priya: confirm a 2-hour window next Tue (Mar 2) for the test and share IP ranges for whitelisting.

Let us know if you'd like a dial-in for the run.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@finlytics.com>, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance SLOs (p95/p99) - recap

Looping in our infra lead to propose concrete test parameters. Proposed perf test plan:
- Test window: 2 hours (as suggested).
- Scenarios:
  1) Interactive streaming: 80-token responses, 1-4 concurrent micro-batches, sustain 60 concurrent sessions, ramp to 200 req/sec for 5-minute spikes. Measure first-byte, p50/p95/p99, and percent of requests hitting >300ms.
  2) Bulk inference (no streaming): 128-token payloads, batch sizes up to 16, measure throughput and cost per 1k tokens.
- Measurement points: end-to-end (client->Redwood->client) from FinLytics test runners in our US West region + server-side traces from Redwood.
- Success criteria: interactive streaming p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 500ms; first-byte < 150ms for >= 90% of requests.

Aditya - can you prepare a perf profile for the two candidate variants (quantized-4 and int8-fused) and include cost delta estimates per 1M tokens? We'll attach the perf profile to the test run doc.

Thanks - Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@finlytics.com>, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance SLOs (p95/p99) - recap

Thanks all - attaching the perf runbook + quick numbers I pulled from recent runs. Quick highlights:
- Candidate model A (quantized-4): median first-byte ~ 95ms, p95 ~ 160ms, p99 ~ 320ms for 80-token streaming responses from us-west region. Cost estimate: $0.85 per 1k tokens.
- Candidate model B (int8-fused): median first-byte ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 200ms, p99 ~ 360ms, better throughput under batching; cost estimate: $0.72 per 1k tokens.

Notes on tuning:
- Enable prefix KV caching for conversational flows (reduces compute for repeated context).
- Use micro-batching (1-4) for streaming routes; increase batch window only for non-interactive bulk jobs.
- For client SDKs, prefer HTTP/2 + keepalive and allow up to 8 concurrent streams per connection.

Next steps:
- Alex/Priya: confirm test window (proposed Tue Mar 2) and provide test runner IP ranges.
- We will provision a temporary dedicated test pool (no billing impact) to run your scenarios and capture server-side traces + p95/p99 breakdowns.

Attaching: redwood-performance-runbook.pdf (summary) and finlytics-current-provider-metrics.csv (your export).

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
